chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Is there a limit for istinja' (cleansing the private parts)?' He said, 'It is not purified as long as there is (something) there.' I said, 'Supposing he cleans what is there, and the wind (of passing gas) remains?' He said, 'The wind is not looked at.'

key_terms.الاسْتِنْجَاءِ: Cleansing the private parts with water after urination or defecation
key_terms.الرِّيحُ: Wind (gas), referring to the sensation or passing of wind

ai.seo_question: What is the limit of cleansing (istinja') in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in ritual purity, where the Imam clarifies that the removal of the physical impurity (*ma'qul*) is the primary condition for cleansing, while the lingering sensation of wind (*rih*) is disregarded (*la yunazal ilayha*). This ruling provides practical relief for believers, distinguishing between tangible impurity and mere sensory perception, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for maintaining *taharah* without excessive doubt (*waswas*).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Al Mugheira, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For the cleansing of the private parts, there is a limit?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not purified for as long as there is (something) there’. I said, ‘Supposing he cleans what is there, and the wind remains?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wind is not something you can look at’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’

How is washing oneself after using the toilet done? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not clean as long as something is there.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if everything there is washed clean but smell is there?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Smell is not a thing that can be seen.’”
